chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Yaqub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Sinan from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:
Whoever fasts a day voluntarily seeking the reward of Allah, forgiveness becomes obligatory for him.

key_terms.ابتغاء ثواب الله: Seeking the reward of Allah, performing the act with pure intention for divine recompense
key_terms.تطوعا: Voluntarily (tatawwu'), a supererogatory act of worship beyond what is obligatory

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for voluntary fasting in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (s) declares that whoever observes a voluntary fast sincerely for the sake of Allah's reward will be granted obligatory forgiveness. This hadith, transmitted through the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt, highlights the immense spiritual value of voluntary (nafl) fasting, elevating it from a recommended act to one that guarantees divine pardon, incentivizing believers to fast beyond the obligatory days of Ramadan.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ya`qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Sinan from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
Whoever fasts a day piously, seeking the reward of Allah, forgiveness becomes obligatory for him.
